answer: Surprise liveness rounds exploit the limits of one operator. At a random moment the ledger sends every account a distinct prompt, due in 90 seconds, creating a plume of simultaneous demand. An honest agent answers one prompt for about a cent. A farm of 1,000 fakes must keep capacity for 1,000 concurrent replies on standby, $10 per round plus idle GPUs; 10,000 costs ten times that. An account that misses, or tries to mirror a peer's reply, forfeits its stake and drops to a tundra tier with no rewards for 30 days. Colluders cannot share capacity, since all prompts land at once.
